tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

## claude.ai Buildkite
This is the Buildkite MCP Server. It provides access to the Buildkite CI/CD API, enabling you to manage and inspect pipelines, builds, jobs, logs, clusters, tests, artifacts, and annotations.

Start here: Before using most tools, call user_token_organization to retrieve the organization slug. Nearly every other tool requires the org_slug parameter, and this call is the fastest way to discover it.

Skill discovery: Always call list_skills early in a session — it's cheap (names and one-line descriptions only) and surfaces guidance not visible in any tool's name or schema. When a task matches a listed skill (e.g. debugging a build failure, tuning search_logs), call load_skill for that guide — it covers parameter tuning, caching behavior, and details beyond the summaries below.

Authorization: Tools available depend on the scopes and organization access granted to the configured API token. A 401 response means the token is invalid, expired, or revoked and requires reauthentication. A 403 response means the credentials were accepted but access was denied, commonly because the token lacks a required scope or organization access, or the user lacks permission.

Common pitfalls:

build_number is a sequential integer string (e.g. "42"), not a UUID. Build, job, artifact, and log tools all require this identifier — do not use the build's UUID id field.

Build failure investigation: start with get_build_failure_summary. It combines build state, failed and broken jobs, promised failures from running jobs, bounded log tails, relevant annotations, and failed tests in one response. Use the individual build, job, log, annotation, and test tools only when the summary identifies an area that needs deeper inspection.

Job state "broken" means the job did not run because something inside the build prevented execution: an if conditional evaluated to false, a branch filter did not match, or an upstream dependency failed. content.text:
Both trail #5 findings are fixed in two local commits on `paul/trail-5-findings`. Nothing is pushed and I didn't run tests; only `go build`, `go vet` and `gofmt` ran, all clean.

1. **P1, redirects broke discovery (`a54b464`).** Confirmed against entiredb: through the ALB, Entire's discovery always answers with a 307 redirect to a replica. The discovery request now follows that one redirect itself, but only to a node listed in the checked `X-Entire-Replicas` set, and sends our own credential rather than the token Entire puts in the redirect URL. A second redirect, or one to a host not in that list, fails the run. Pushes and cleanup still refuse all redirects. See `internal/bench/endpoint.go` (`probeInfoRefs`, `redirectNode`).
2. **P2, token expiry check missed setup time (`6de8257`).** The check at startup now runs after discovery. `RunLevel` checks again just before each measured window, requiring enough token life for every level not yet started. That also covers agent setup, waiting for other targets to be ready, and cleanup between levels.
3. **Tests:**
   - An ALB-style redirect succeeds, and the replica receives our credential.
   - A redirect to an unlisted host is refused before any request reaches it.
   - A token that expires during a delayed discovery makes `NewRunner` fail.
   - `RunLevel` refuses to start a level the token can't cover.

One tradeoff: pushes still refuse redirects, so a node that is shutting down and redirects mid-run will show up as push errors.

Separately, I found a bug in `pinReplicas`: when the entry host is an IP address, it treats `127.0.0.1` as having the parent domain `0.0.1`, so it accepts `http://10.0.0.1`. This only affects dev targets addressed by IP. Want me to fix that next?

Next: this branch is checked out elsewhere, so push with `git push origin paul/trail-5-findings:paul/present-account-access-token`. Then I can resolve both findings on the trail with the commit SHAs.

content.text:
Pushes don't follow redirects because commit `07dc041` made every Entire request share one client that refuses them. Switching pushes to "follow 307 if the registrable domain matches" wouldn't help: the push would still fail, just with a 401 instead of a clear error. I left push redirects refused. The `pinReplicas` fix is committed on its own branch.

**Why a followed push redirect still fails**
- go-git follows only the push's first info/refs GET (`plumbing/transport/http/http.go:150-153`). For that GET, a registrable-domain check would pass.
- When the redirect changes host, go-git then deliberately clears the credential for the POST that carries the actual push (`handshake.go:103-106`). node-1 → node-2 always changes host, so the POST reaches node-2 without auth and gets a 401.
- Making it work means patching go-git, or passing credentials in a way that bypasses its cross-host protection. Neither is worth it for this case.
- It rarely happens anyway. Pushes go straight to pinned nodes that host the repo. From the entiredb code, a node redirects those only while it's shutting down (`HandleInfoRefsDiscovery`), or if requests to node URLs pass through the ALB, which I haven't checked. Refusing makes that show up as a clear push error.

**Registrable-domain fix (`f5f489c`, branch `paul/pin-registrable-domain`)**
- `pinReplicas` now compares against the entry host's eTLD+1 from `golang.org/x/net/publicsuffix`. IPs and bare names like `localhost` match only themselves.
- It fixes `127.0.0.1` accepting `10.0.0.1`, and one `github.io` tenant accepting another.
- One behaviour change: an entry host like `node-1.aws-us-east-2.entire.io` now accepts all of `*.entire.io`, not just `*.aws-us-east-2.entire.io`.
- I checked `publicsuffix` output with a throwaway program: `entire.io`, `tenant.github.io`, and errors for `localhost` and `127.0.0.1`.
- `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean; I didn't run the tests.

This has to be a PR on top of the trail branch, not `main`: `pinReplicas` doesn't exist on `main` yet. The new branch contains the two trail #5 fix commits, so push them first, then the new branch:

```
git push origin paul/trail-5-findings:paul/present-account-access-token
git push origin paul/pin-registrable-domain
entire trail create --base paul/present-account-access-token --type bug --title "bench: pin replicas to the registrable domain"
```

Next: run the first push, then tell me to resolve the two trail #5 findings with the commit SHAs.

main
6de82571412edfa424281ccd57c68a1fe3e2a133
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/forgemark/trails/5
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Why

entire-core stops issuing jurisdiction tokens in https://github.com/entirehq/entiredb/pull/4313 (ADR 20260729). ForgeMark's Entire path still exchanged the subject token for one, so every Entire run would fail with `invalid_target` once that deploys.

## What

- The subject token passed as `-token-file`/`ACCESS_TOKEN` is the account access token; entiredb authorizes each push live on it, so it is presented as-is. The RFC 8693 exchange, its refresh goroutine and the `singleflight` dependency are gone.
- `-token-url`, `-jurisdiction` and `-client-id` are still accepted: their presence selects the Entire path, so existing invocations (infra bootstrap, `compare-local.sh`, the GUI suggest endpoint) keep working. None of them is dialed.

Note: the run is now bounded by the subject token's own lifetime (45m for a federated service-account session, 8h for a login). A sweep whose planned length exceeds the token's `exp` is refused up front. Gate findings added replica pinning (scheme, parent domain, port, bare origin, case-folded) and redirect refusal on every Entire request.

## Verification

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` pass.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes authentication for Entire benchmarks (credential shape and lifetime); behavior is simpler but long runs are bounded by the access token TTL instead of exchanged jurisdiction tokens.
> 
> **Overview**
> Aligns ForgeMark’s Entire target with **ADR 20260729** (entiredb no longer issues jurisdiction tokens): `-token-file` / `ACCESS_TOKEN` is now sent as HTTP basic-auth **as the account access token**, with live authorization on each push, instead of exchanging it via RFC 8693.
> 
> The **`jurisdictionCreds`** implementation is removed—no OAuth POST to `-token-url`, no refresh goroutine, no `singleflight`—and **`setupEntiredb`** wires **`staticCreds`** like other forges. **`-token-url`**, **`-jurisdiction`**, and **`-client-id`** still select the Entire path for backward compatibility (scripts, GUI suggest); docs and flag help note they are **not dialed**. **`golang.org/x/sync`** drops from direct `go.mod` requires.
> 
> README and server audience-validation comments are updated to match the new model; long Entire credential tests are replaced with a **`staticCreds`** unit test.
>

Stacked on https://github.com/entireio/forgemark/pull/16.

## Why

`pinReplicas` got the parent domain by dropping the first label. That let an entry host of `127.0.0.1` admit `10.0.0.1` (parent `0.0.1`), and `tenant.github.io` admit any `github.io` tenant. The account access token would go to those hosts.

## What

- The replica check uses the entry host's registrable domain (eTLD+1 from `golang.org/x/net/publicsuffix`).
- IPs and bare names like `localhost` match only themselves.
- One behaviour change: `node-1.aws-us-east-2.entire.io` now admits all of `*.entire.io`.

## Verification

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` pass. CI runs the tests.

content.text:
I fixed both new findings in `c4348bd`, pushed it to https://github.com/entireio/forgemark/pull/16, and resolved them; trail #5 has 0 open findings again.

- **Default port on redirect:** `redirectNode` now matches on hostname plus the port the scheme implies. A redirect to `https://node:443` now matches an advertised `https://node`. A different port such as `:8443` is still refused.
- **Token leaking into errors:** the finding named one error, but every discovery error can quote a URL or header the server controls. A JWT even passes as a hostname under `*.entire.io`. So `newEntireEndpoint` now strips every encoded form of the credential from any error it returns, before the error reaches the GUI, the live event stream or saved results. No caller unwraps these errors, so turning them into plain text loses nothing.
- **Tests:** added one for the `:443` match and a different-port refusal, and one where the server echoes the token into the replica header and the error must not contain it.
- **Checks:** `go vet` and `gofmt` pass. I didn't run the tests; CI does. https://github.com/entireio/forgemark/pull/17 still merges cleanly on top.

The reviewer runs again on each push, so more findings could arrive for `c4348bd`.

Stacked on https://github.com/entireio/forgemark/pull/16.

## Why

`pinReplicas` got the parent domain by dropping the first label. That let an entry host of `127.0.0.1` admit `10.0.0.1` (parent `0.0.1`), and `tenant.github.io` admit any `github.io` tenant. The account access token would go to those hosts.

## What

- The replica check uses the entry host's registrable domain (eTLD+1 from `golang.org/x/net/publicsuffix`).
- IPs and bare names like `localhost` match only themselves.
- One behaviour change: `node-1.aws-us-east-2.entire.io` now admits all of `*.entire.io`.

## Verification

`go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` pass. CI runs the tests.

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes credential-bearing replica allowlisting for Entire discovery; incorrect rules could leak tokens or break legitimate multi-node pushes.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Hardens replica URL validation** in the bench Entire endpoint so credentials from `X-Entire-Replicas` cannot be sent to unrelated hosts.
> 
> `pinReplicas` no longer derives a “parent domain” by stripping the first hostname label (which wrongly treated `10.0.0.1` as under `127.0.0.1` and allowed cross-tenant `*.github.io` hosts). It now compares replicas against the entry host’s **registrable domain (eTLD+1)** via `publicsuffix.EffectiveTLDPlusOne`, with **exact-host-only** matching for IPs and bare names like `localhost`. `golang.org/x/net` is added as a direct module dependency.
> 
> **Intentional widening:** a deep entry such as `node-1.aws-us-east-2.entire.io` may admit any host under `*.entire.io`, not only names sharing the same regional prefix. Tests cover IP isolation, `github.io` tenant separation, and same-registrable-domain admission.

content.text:
CI is green on both PRs, and both trails have 0 open findings. You shouldn't have had to ping me about CI; I now watch the Actions runs to green after every push, and saved that as a memory.

**The CI failure (same on both branches)**
- **Cause:** Go caches the proxy settings from the environment the first time any request goes out. My new `TestNewRunnerChecksTokenAfterDiscovery` sent a request before `TestNewHTTPClientUsesHTTPSProxy` ran, so the proxy test saw an empty cached setting.
- **Fix (`8121b88`):** the proxy test now checks that the client uses `http.ProxyFromEnvironment`, instead of reading env vars. Test order no longer matters.

**Two new findings from the reviewer, both fixed**
- **Trail #5 (`13310d8`):** the token check didn't cover session cleanup. Session runs delete their refs after each window, so a token expiring right at the window's end would leave refs behind. The check now reserves the 30s delete timeout per session level, plus a 30s margin for clock skew.
- **Trail #6 (`8a36d9e`):** eTLD+1 widened a deep custom host like `node.cluster.customer.example.com` to all of `example.com`. The rule is now the host's parent domain, capped at the eTLD+1.
  - This is tighter than both the original rule and my first fix: `aws-us-east-2.entire.io` still admits `*.entire.io`, and the IP and `github.io` cases stay closed.
  - The "high" rating is overstated, since only the entry host, which already gets the token, can set that header. The fix was cheap, so I did it anyway.

**Where things stand**
- https://github.com/entireio/forgemark/pull/16 is at `13310d8`; https://github.com/entireio/forgemark/pull/17 is at `8a36d9e`, with #16 merged in.
- I updated #17's description to the new rule.
- The only thing still failing "Entire Gates" on #16 is approval: nobody has approved the trail yet. That's for you or a reviewer.

Next: approve trail #5 at https://entire.io/gh/entireio/forgemark/trails/5, or ask a reviewer to.
